findings.claim: status.json mint.main / permit.readable / permit.invariant: mint_readable, permit_readable, supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit hold for every successful call.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Each of these takes hsep : Sep (callKeys message), a keccak hypothesis that is never discharged and never shown satisfiable (it would need 2^160 keccak evaluations). So no closed instance of mint_readable, permit_readable or any supply_* theorem exists; the Sanity witnesses (mint_runs and Sanity/Zero) witness only the raw path theorems, which do not need Sep. Sep is local to the three address words of the call and I found no contradiction among its fields, so this is the usual disclosed caveat, not a false hypothesis. One thing the status wording hides: Sep says nothing about an allowance slot or a nonce slot being slot 0, 1 or 11 (only: not a balance slot, not slot 4, allowance != nonce). The per-call statements stay honest (approve_readable and permit_readable only say 'every slot other than the written ones is kept'), but any reading such as 'approve or permit never changes the owner or lastMintTimestamp' needs that extra keccak fact, which is not in Sep.
evidence: token-kit/tokens/ena/EnaVerify/Ena/Sep.lean:68-81 (structure Sep: total, uniq, allow, nonce, fixed; 'fixed : Supply.NotBal 2 0 ∧ Supply.NotBal 2 1 ∧ Supply.NotBal 2 11' is about balance slots only)
token-kit/tokens/ena/EnaVerify/Ena/PermitSeq.lean:300-305 (permit_readable ... (hsep : Sep (callKeys message))) and :337-339 (other slots kept only for k != nonce slot, k != allowance slot)
status.json assumptions[0] (disclosed: 'Hypothesis on keccak, not proved')
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Sep (or a second structure) that allowance and nonce slots of the call keys are not 0, 1, 11, and state it in status.json. Say in the status file that no closed instance of a Sep theorem exists.

findings.claim: status.json contract_findings: 'at most once per 365 days', 'supply can grow by at most 10 percent per 365 days through mint', 'only the owner can mint'. README headline: 'mint rules'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: The mint rules are proved per call only. mint_readable: IF one frame of CODE with selector 0x40c10f19 ends with no error THEN caller = low 160 bits of slot 0, lastMint + 31536000 <= block time, amount <= 10 * totalSupply / 100, and the exact writes and logs. That part is solid and matches the bytes (pc 1366 to 1693: onlyOwner at 0x120c, TIMESTAMP - (slot11 & 0xffffffffff) < 0x01e13380 reverts ea0c9af5, amount > totalSupply * 10 / 100 reverts c507dd3b, SSTORE slot 11, _mint at 0x128e, LOG2 Mint). What is NOT a theorem: (a) any statement over a sequence of calls about slot 11 or slot 4, so 'at most 10 percent per 365 days' and 'once per 365 days' are inferences, not Lean results; (b) a single theorem that no other function raises totalSupply or writes slot 11 or slot 0 (the kit has gen_nomint.py; ENA does not use it; it follows function by function from the readable theorems only with Sep plus the extra keccak facts of ENA-1); (c) the failing side (the 11 revert paths exist one by one, with no 'a mint that breaks a rule reverts with this error' summary; disclosed). My byte census agrees with the informal claim: 12 SSTORE, slot 11 written only at pc 1599, slot 4 only at pc 4895 (_mint) and 5390 (_burn), _mint (0x128e) is jumped to only from pc 1605, and the mint body (0x556) only from the dispatcher (pc 622).
evidence: ENA.txt (audit scratch, not kept) pc 1366-1693, 4875-4942, 5382-5390; grep 'PUSH2 128e' gives one site (pc 1605)
token-kit/scripts/gen_nomint.py exists; tokens/ena/config/ena.json generators = code, dispatch, paths, loops, supply, readable, sanity, axioms (no nomint)
findings.suggested_fix: Either mark the two rate sentences as 'read from the bytes, per call; no sequence theorem', or add a sequence theorem: along CallsP, totalSupply at the end <= totalSupply at the start * 1.1^(number of mint steps), and two successful mints are at least 31536000 seconds apart (needs block time in the step and the keccak facts of ENA-1).

findings.claim: status.json permit.main: ok_permit_real proves permit under EthLib's real runner with nothing assumed about the precompile; permit.invariant: every top-level message with any selector, permit included.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: Proved in one direction only: IF a fresh frame of CODE with selector 0xd505accf ends with no error under processRunner, with .shapella <= fork < .glamsterdam and hdel (no EIP-7702 delegation code at address 1), THEN the checks hold and PermitDone holds (recovered word = EthLib's Precompiles.Ecrecover.compute on digest, v, r, s; not 0; equal to owner; nonce + 1; allowance = value; one Approval log). The digest is faithful: I recomputed PERMIT_TYPEHASH, the domain type hash, keccak('ENA'), keccak('1'), CACHED_DOMAIN = rebuilt hash for chain 1 and the deployed address, P1901, half n; all are in the bytes. EthLib's compute is real secp256k1 recovery (not a stub, no opaque). But: (a) there is no witness and no forward theorem, so nothing in Lean shows that a successful permit exists in the model; ok_permit_real, supply_permit, permit_readable, PermitCall and the permit arm of process_step_all could all be vacuous as far as the kernel knows (I do not believe they are: permit_p8/p10/p12 and the tail success paths are forward theorems, only the forward call rule and a signature are missing); (b) hdel / NoDelegation1 is never discharged for any state; (c) runs where hdel fails or fork >= glamsterdam are outside every permit theorem, including the 'any selector' sequence theorems (process_step_all needs hglam and hdel even for non-permit selectors). All three are disclosed in not_covered / assumptions; the gap is that 'permit included' reads stronger than 'a conditional with no instance'.

findings.claim: status.json permit.invariant and Seq.lean: the supply invariant holds 'along every sequence' / for 'every top-level message'.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: True inside the Calls / CallsP model. A step is (1) GoodCall: a fresh frame of CODE run by processRunner that ends with no error, any selector but permit, with Sep; (2) PermitCall; or (3) 'other': Untouched, which is ASSUMED (every storage word of C kept). process_step and process_step_all show that one processMessage run with message.code = CODE and precompileAddress = none is a step of kind 1, 2 or (on error, proved by rollback) 3. Not linked: a whole transaction (EthLib's processTransaction), an outer frame that reverts after a successful inner call to the token, and anything else that is not such a message, all of which the user must put in 'other' by assumption. Inv at the start of a sequence is assumed, never established (no deployment or constructor state; disclosed). All 26 selectors are covered: supply_preserved matches on the 26 entries, renounceOwnership by ok_renounceOwnership : False, short data, unknown selector and value sent by ends_ok_dispatch, permit by supply_permit. Nothing is excluded by selector, which is better than BNB in the QNT, BNB and WETH audit.
findings.suggested_fix: State the model limits next to the headline. Optional: lift to processTransaction, or prove Untouched for a message whose target is not C and that makes no call.

findings.claim: status.json assumptions[1]: 'every theorem needs .shapella <= fork'; only permit is bounded by fork < .glamsterdam.
findings.what_is_actually_proved: All non-permit theorems (mint_readable, supply_preserved, ok_<fn>, process_step, inv_calls) are stated for Evm fork Nat, the one-counter meter, for every fork from Shapella with no upper bound. EthLib runs forks from Glamsterdam with StateGasMeter (and step-level rules change there: checkGas), so for fork >= .glamsterdam these theorems are about a meter EthLib does not use for real execution. They are true statements, but they do not describe ENA on a Glamsterdam chain. Mainnet at the audited block is before Glamsterdam, so nothing is wrong today. Same finding as SHIB F2.

token-kit/tokens/ena/EnaVerify/Ena/Seq.lean:66-72 (GoodCall: evm s : Evm fork Nat, .shapella <= fork, no upper bound)
findings.suggested_fix: Add fork < .glamsterdam to the headline wording (or to the theorems), as permit already has.

findings.claim: Worth telling the owner (true behaviour of the deployed bytes, confirmed by the proofs and by my reading of the bytes).
findings.what_is_actually_proved: 1. Only the address in slot 0 can mint; there is no other minter role and no other entry to _mint. 2. A mint needs block time >= lastMintTimestamp + 365 days and amount <= floor(totalSupply * 10 / 100) at call time; the cap compounds (each mint raises the next cap) and a burn lowers it. 3. mint(to, 0) is allowed and restarts the 365-day wait, so the owner can burn a year's mint right with one call. 4. If lastMintTimestamp is ever above the block time the mint reverts with Panic 0x11 (checked subtraction). The first allowed mint time depends on the value the constructor stored in slot 11, which the proof does not model and I did not read from chain. 5. lastMintTimestamp keeps only 40 bits of the block time (wraps in year 36812, no practical effect). 6. renounceOwnership() always reverts (after the owner check), so the mint right can not be dropped that way; ownership moves only by transferOwnership then acceptOwnership by the pending owner. transferOwnership has no zero-address check: transferOwnership(0) just clears the pending owner. 7. totalSupply add in mint is checked; the receiver balance add and the totalSupply sub in burn are unchecked and safe only because sum of balances = totalSupply. 8. burnFrom and transferFrom do not lower an allowance of 2^256 - 1. 9. permit: nonce is incremented before the ECRECOVER call; high s and a zero recovered address are rejected; the domain separator is rebuilt when chain id or address differ from the cached ones. 10. No pause, blacklist, fee or hook; the only outside call in the whole code is the STATICCALL to address 1.
